title: Instructions vs Examples
summary: Examples teach AI the shape — adjectives alone are not enough.

sections.heading: Orientation — Beginning of the Lesson
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? When to describe with words and when to show an example — and how this affects the quality of AI outputs in your product.
- Why now? Many Prompts fail not because AI is 'weak' — but because you described it with adjectives ('professional', 'creative') instead of showing the shape.
- What after the lesson? You will write a Prompt that includes two examples + a clear pattern line.

sections.heading: Tension — Detailed Explanation — and Any Response
sections.subtitle: Detailed Explanation — and Any Response
sections.contentMarkdown:
- I wrote 'Write in an engaging and unique style' — and the response was clichés: 'Discover the magic' and 'A unique experience'.
- AI is better at mimicking than understanding general adjectives.
- When you build a feature (titles, support responses, interface cards): two correct examples = a consistent style for all users.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Example Teaches Better than Adjective
sections.subtitle: Example Teaches Better than Adjective
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Instructions = Steps or rules in words: 'Do 1, 2, 3'.
- Examples = Show the shape of the response you want: 'Do like this and this'.
- AI mimics patterns. One or two examples are stronger than 100 adjectives ('short', 'friendly', 'creative').
- In Builder: when you ask Lovable 'Create 4 cards like this card' — this is Few-shot Prompting. The same idea applies to any Prompt.

sections.heading: Comparison — Description vs Example — Same Request
sections.subtitle: Description vs Example — Same Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Description in words | Example to mimic |
|---------------------|------------------|
| 'Write me 3 catchy titles for honey product.' — Often 'Golden Bee Honey' and 'Healing from Nature' — General words | 'Write me 3 titles for honey, in the style of: 'Liquid gold from nature'.' — All responses are poetic like the example |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms to Start
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| Instructions | Rules and steps in words — suitable for organized tasks | 'Read the article → Identify 3 ideas → Summarize each in one line.' |
| Few-shot Prompting | Gives AI 2–3 examples of the desired shape before the actual request | Two emails to respond to customers + 'Write a response to the new email in the same style.' |

sections.heading: Screenshot Block (Intent)
sections.contentMarkdown: Matching Cards — From One Example: The cards all have the same format. Not from long instructions — from one example: 'Create a card like this for other paths.' AI understood the pattern and mimicked it.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You want posts in the same style: 'A balanced breakfast makes your day better'. What is the best way?
Give 2–3 examples in the same style (Few-shot).
Write long instructions about 'the sentence structure'.
Just tell them to write posts about habits and that's it.
Explanation: When the shape is hard to describe — examples establish the pattern. This is the basis of any content feature in your product.

sections.heading: Mission — Two Examples + Pattern — For the Same Request
sections.subtitle: Two Examples + Pattern — For the Same Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Weak request → Add two examples + pattern sentence. 10–15 minutes is enough. Delivery: 1. Weak request: 'Write me 3 ideas for a podcast about entrepreneurship'
2. Improved request — Add: - Example 1 (Idea + Title) - Example 2 (Idea + Title) - Pattern line: 'Write me 3 ideas in the same style'
3. What pattern did the examples teach? (One sentence) Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Consistent examples | 60% | The examples are in the same style; there is a clear pattern line |
| Pattern analysis | 40% | Described the pattern — not just 'it got better'; usable in Product Prompt |
